scraped.scraped_description: Open Referral UK is a open data standard which makes it easy to publish, find and use community services data.

name: Open Referral UK
tagline: The open data standard that makes it easy to publish, find, and use community services data.
known_funders: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government (MHCLG)

awards.name: Central Digital and Data Office Endorsement
awards.description: Recommended standard for community services data

policy_outcomes.description: Endorsed by the Central Digital and Data Office as a recommended standard for community services data in UK local government
Adopted by multiple UK local councils including Bristol City Council and Buckinghamshire Council for Family Information Services

published_performance_metrics: adoption metrics and case studies available on project website
documented_limitations: Voluntary adoption by councils limits standardization
Data quality depends on publisher compliance
Limited cross-sector integration beyond social care
governance_model: Steering Group with government and community representation; versioned releases
curation_criteria: compliance criteria published; validator tool available
disparity_tracking: Equity considerations in service accessibility; focus on reducing information barriers for vulnerable populations
community_ownership: Community organisations and councils participate in governance; open contribution model

government_partnerships.partner: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government

ai_involvement: No AI/machine learning components; standard data format specification
political_relevance_summary: Open Referral UK addresses fragmentation in community service information, making it easier for residents to find and access support services through standardized open data.

movement_building_utility.notes: Open Referral UK's primary function is not directly oriented toward civic organizing, advocacy, or movement infrastructure.

generalizability_notes: Moderate generalizability. Open Referral UK is open source but designed for UK-specific regulatory and institutional contexts. Adaptation to other jurisdictions would require significant localization.
